display.purpose: Screen title in the screen head; always uppercase. 2rem on phones; mission and arcade titles 2.25rem.

headline.purpose: World name on the sector plate and dialog titles; uppercase.

title.purpose: Panel titles, roster mode names, arcade task names; uppercase.

console.purpose: Rail items, teacher tabs and briefing summaries; uppercase.

action.purpose: Hazard slabs: Deploy at 1.375rem, Next mission at 1.125rem; uppercase.

numeral.purpose: Every count, score and index, tabular, in a fixed cell or row slot.

body.purpose: Descriptions, instructions and coach text, 62 to 70ch; sentence case.

label.purpose: Readout captions, table headers, field names and row state words; uppercase.

code.purpose: Editor, queue, trace, compiler feedback and combat answers.

shadows.name: hairline
shadows.purpose: Edge of every panel, plate and readout cell; survives the chamfer clip.

shadows.name: status-rim
shadows.purpose: Status line edge; switches to a 55% danger rim on error.

shadows.name: dialog-lift
shadows.purpose: Dialogs over the flat rgba(4,6,9,.8) scrim; no backdrop blur.

shadows.name: sheet-lift
shadows.purpose: Phone More sheet above the bottom bar.

shadows.name: agent-glow
shadows.purpose: The agent tile; one of the only two glows in the system.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: Every CSS transition and keyframe in the shell.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Background, border and colour changes on controls; disclosure chevron rotation.

motion.name: area-swap
motion.purpose: Rail brand and spine changing area colour between screens.

motion.name: piece-arrive
motion.purpose: Agent render settling on its new tile.

motion.name: table-turn
motion.purpose: War table turning the chosen world forward; selected planet scales .5 to .64. The one long move.

motion.name: reduced
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion or the in-game Reduce motion toggle: all transitions and animations instant; the table stops its ambient bob and sweep and turns instantly.

components.name: Hazard Primary Button
components.description: The one pressable primary action in a region (Compile and run, Export, Next mission). Disabled drops the yellow.

components.name: Console Button
components.description: Default pill control for every secondary action; flat, no glow, 1px press.

components.name: Warn Ghost Button
components.description: Destructive or reset action: transparent pill with an Alarm Red edge.

Logic Labyrinth

World 01 of 05

Build your first algorithms and navigate digital mazes.

1 / 3 solved

narrative.overview:
The whole game is one console on a starship bridge. A hull off-black room, gunmetal plates and a console rail of warm colour-block elbows frame a single lit object: the holo war table, a real-time WebGL disc carrying five Blender-rendered planets. The mission grid is that same table zoomed in, so the board, the route trace and the status line share its hologram blue, and nothing else in the room glows. Chrome stays flat, dark and quiet so the student's code and the board are always the brightest things on screen.

Density is a working console, not a poster: 40 to 64px controls, real numbers in fixed readout cells, list rows instead of card grids, and every panel either squared or chamfered against the dark. Colour does three separate jobs and never trades them: the area colour says where you are, hazard yellow says what to press, hologram blue says this is the table. Motion is short and mechanical; the one long move is the table turning a world forward, and reduced motion makes all of it instant.

The world takes its cues from bridge consoles and drop-pod tactical screens but borrows no franchise logos, names, fonts or assets. It rejects the stacked glowing-button space menu, grids of identical mode cards, and glass panels.
keyCharacteristics: Hull off-black ground with four tonal hull steps and 1px inset hairlines; no decorative gradients in chrome.
One lit object: the holo war table and the mission board that is its zoomed-in view.
Colour jobs split three ways: area colour for wayfinding, hazard yellow for pressing, hologram blue for the table.
Three geometries: 45-degree chamfered plates, pill and elbow console controls, 4px machined slabs.
Antonio condensed caps for the console's voice, Barlow for reading, JetBrains Mono for code, tabular numerals in fixed cells.
Blender renders for every planet, piece, mode emblem and fighter; Tabler outline icons at 2px stroke; no emoji.
Short mechanical motion that goes instant under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Hazard Means Press Rule
rules.body: Hazard yellow fills only something you can press that moves you forward, one per region. It never decorates, never marks a secondary action and never survives on a disabled control.

rules.name: The Table Owns the Blue Rule
rules.body: Hologram blue belongs to the war table, the planets, the mission board, the route trace and the status line, plus the focus ring. The rail, panels, headings and resting buttons never take it.

rules.name: The Wayfinding Only Rule
rules.body: An area colour tells you where you are and what is selected inside that area. It never fills a primary action and never appears in another area's chrome.

rules.name: The Console Voice Rule
rules.body: Antonio is always uppercase and only for what the console names: titles, rail items, action words and numerals. Sentences are Barlow in sentence case.

rules.name: The Fixed Cell Rule
rules.body: Every number that changes sets in tabular numerals in a fixed cell or row slot, so a ticking score never shifts its neighbours.

rules.name: The Code Is Mono Rule
rules.body: Code, the move queue, the trace, compiler feedback and combat answer options set in JetBrains Mono; nothing else does.

rules.name: The Hairline Edge Rule
rules.body: Panels separate by a tonal step and a 1px inset hairline, never by a cast shadow. Shadows belong to things that float over the deck: dialogs and the overflow sheet.

rules.name: The Board Glows Alone Rule
rules.body: Glow exists only on the mission board's goal and agent tiles. Chrome never glows.

rules.name: The Three Geometries Rule
rules.body: Plates chamfer, console controls pill or elbow, slabs inside a plate take the 4px machined corner. Panels are never softly rounded; there is no 8 to 24px card radius anywhere in the system.

rules.name: The Counted Progress Rule
rules.body: A count of missions or challenges is drawn as lit skewed segments with the number printed beside it ("0 / 3 solved"), never as an unlabelled smooth bar.

dos: Do open every screen with the screen head: area cap, uppercase Antonio title, one Barlow line, and real numbers in a readout strip.
Do set one area per screen (Campaign Amber, Arcade Lilac, Combat Coral, Teacher Steel) and let the rail, cap, underline and selection inherit it.
Do give the one pressable primary action in a region Hazard Yellow (#ffd21f) with Ink text, and drop it to Hull Control with Caption Grey when disabled.
Do separate panels with a tonal step and a 1px inset hairline (`box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--line)`).
Do chamfer tactical plates at 14px, pill the console controls, and give slabs inside a plate the 4px corner.
Do count progress in lit skewed segments with the count printed beside them.
Do pair every status colour with a word: Solved, Next up, Code required, or a plain-language error.
Do use Blender renders for planets, pieces, mode emblems and fighters, each shipped with its provenance record, and Tabler outline icons at 2px stroke for everything else.

Do keep motion at 0.3s or less on the cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1) ease, with the 720ms table turn as the one long move, and make all of it instant under reduced motion from the system or the in-game toggle.
Do hold every text pair at WCAG AA; Caption Grey (#8d99a3) is the lowest text tone allowed on any hull.
donts: Don't fill or tint the rail, panels, headings or resting buttons with Hologram Blue; it belongs to the table, planets, board, trace, status line and focus ring.
Don't use an area colour for a primary action, or one area's colour in another area's chrome.
Don't put Hazard Yellow on anything that cannot be pressed, on secondary buttons, or on disabled controls.
Don't round panels softly; there is no 8 to 24px card radius.
Don't add glows, text-shadows, filters or hover lift to chrome; glow belongs to the goal and agent tiles alone.
Don't use backdrop blur or translucent glass panels; dialogs sit on a flat 80% scrim.
Don't put kickers or eyebrows above headings; the shell hides them outright.
Don't use emoji or text glyphs as icons or game pieces; they become Blender sprites or Tabler icons.
Don't lay modes out as a grid of identical glowing cards; use the roster row.
Don't set paragraphs in Antonio or in uppercase.
Don't use franchise logos, names, fonts or copied assets; Star Trek and Helldivers are inspiration only.
